trapAlert: MS-PCR diagnoses PWS (>99% sensitive), but CANNOT tell WHY! You must do Microarray/MLPA to tell whether it's a microdeletion (70%), maternal UPD (25%), or an imprinting center defect (which carries a massive 50% RECURRENCE RISK)!

subject: Biology
subtopic: Non-Mendelian inheritance patterns comparative pedigree analysis
question:
A medical genetics seminar analyzes four independent clinical pedigrees, each displaying a distinct departure from classical Mendelian inheritance:
• Pedigree 1: A progressive neurological disorder displays earlier age of onset and increasing choreic severity in successive generations, with massive severe expansions occurring when transmitted by affected fathers.
• Pedigree 2: A metabolic encephalomyopathy is transmitted by an affected woman to all four of her children (with varying severity from mild deafness to fatal lactic acidosis), but her affected brother transmits the condition to none of his six children.
• Pedigree 3: A neurodevelopmental disorder manifests in a child whose parents are healthy; molecular analysis shows two normal-copy chromosomes 15 that both derive entirely from the mother with zero paternal contribution.
• Pedigree 4: An intellectual disability syndrome with macroorchidism in males is transmitted through unaffected carrier females whose fathers had a mild late-onset tremor-ataxia syndrome.
Which row correctly matches Pedigrees 1 through 4 to their underlying genetic mechanism?
options: A. 1: Genomic Imprinting; 2: Autosomal Recessive with Isodisomy; 3: Mitochondrial Heteroplasmy; 4: Dynamic CAG Polyglutamine Expansion.
B. 1: X-linked Recessive Lethality; 2: Robertsonian Translocation; 3: Triplet Repeat Anticipation; 4: Uniparental Disomy.

C. 1: Genetic Anticipation via dynamic CAG triplet repeat expansion (Huntington's disease); 2: Mitochondrial DNA inheritance with heteroplasmy (MELAS/MERRF); 3: Maternal Uniparental Disomy via trisomy rescue (Prader-Willi syndrome); 4: X-linked dynamic CGG repeat expansion with premutation carrier status (Fragile X / FXTAS).
D. 1: Somatic Mosaicism; 2: Autosomal Dominant Incomplete Penetrance; 3: Paternal Heterodisomy; 4: Mitochondrial Homoplasmy.
E. 1: Dynamic CTG Toxic RNA Splicingopathy; 2: Meiotic Crossing Over in Inversion Loops; 3: Balanced Reciprocal Translocation; 4: Autosomal Recessive GAA Triplex DNA.
explanation:
1. Legitimizing Principle: Non-Mendelian inheritance patterns encompass dynamic mutations (anticipation), mitochondrial inheritance (maternal transmission and heteroplasmy), genomic imprinting, uniparental disomy, and mosaicism.

2. Step-by-Step Proof:
• Pedigree 1 Analysis: Earlier onset and increasing severity in successive generations with paternal expansion bias is the definition of Genetic Anticipation driven by dynamic CAG repeat expansion in Huntington's disease (HTT gene).
• Pedigree 2 Analysis: Transmission from an affected female to all offspring (100% maternal transmission) combined with zero transmission from an affected male, accompanied by variable clinical severity in offspring, is the hallmark of Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) inheritance with heteroplasmy (as seen in MELAS, MERRF).
• Pedigree 3 Analysis: Normal chromosomal copy number with both homologues of chromosome 15 inherited from the mother and none from the father defines Maternal Uniparental Disomy (mUPD15), a classic mechanism of Prader-Willi syndrome arising from trisomy rescue.
• Pedigree 4 Analysis: Intellectual disability with macroorchidism in boys (Fragile X full mutation >200 CGG) transmitted through normal carrier females (premutation 55-200 CGG) whose fathers had tremor/ataxia (Fragile X-associated Tremor/Ataxia Syndrome [FXTAS] seen in premutation males) defines X-linked dynamic CGG repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene.
• Matching these four exact mechanisms points unequivocally to Option C.

3. Distractor Elimination:
• Option A incorrectly identifies Pedigree 1 as imprinting and Pedigree 2 as autosomal recessive.
• Option B confuses anticipation with translocation and misidentifies mitochondrial inheritance.
• Option D misidentifies Pedigree 1 as somatic mosaicism and Pedigree 2 as incomplete penetrance.
• Option E misattributes Pedigree 1 to CTG splicingopathy and Pedigree 2 to meiotic inversion loops.
trapAlert: Master non-Mendelian pedigree recognition: 1) Huntington = anticipation (CAG, paternal expansion); 2) Mitochondrial = mother transmits to all, father to NONE; 3) UPD = two copies from one parent, zero from other; 4) Fragile X = X-linked CGG premutation/full mutation!
